Do you think I'd actually be able to spot it?

Yes—very likely, assuming a clear, unobstructed northeastern horizon.

An 88% illuminated Moon is extremely bright and should be readily visible during nautical twilight. At an altitude of only **5.3°**, however, it is quite low—roughly the width of three fingers held at arm’s length above the horizon—at an azimuth of **60°**, or **east-northeast**.

The main obstacles would be:

- buildings, hills, or trees blocking the low horizon;
- haze or thin cloud near the horizon;
- atmospheric extinction, which will dim and redden it somewhat.

From a spot with a good view toward the east-northeast—especially somewhere elevated or facing the coast—you should be able to spot it unaided. It will also be rising, so waiting 10–20 minutes should make it noticeably easier to see.
